notes: Starter pack for Singapore GST, corporate income tax, and non-resident withholding. It is a software reference, not a filing position. Reviewed against the cited IRAS and AGC pages on 2026-11-13.

semantic_mappings.rule: Use for supplies that take the generally applicable positive GST rate under GST Act s 16, other than supplies collected under the Overseas Vendor Registration regime.
Use for exports of goods and international services zero-rated under GST Act s 21. Input tax remains creditable.

Use for Fourth Schedule exempt supplies (residential property, prescribed financial services, investment precious metals, digital payment tokens). Input tax is not creditable unless the De Minimis Rule is met or Regulation 33 of the GST (General) Regulations allows the claim. Read see_citation before denying the credit.
Use when the transaction is not a supply for GST, including third-country sales, TOGC, and supplies outside Singapore.
Use when the GST-registered recipient must account for GST on imported services or low-value goods under s 14, typically because the person is not entitled to full input tax credit.

Use for B2C imported digital services, remote non-digital services, or low-value goods on which an overseas vendor (or marketplace/redeliverer) collects the prevailing standard GST rate under the Overseas Vendor Registration regime. Do not use reverse_charge for this collection path.
Use for the flat 17% corporate income tax on chargeable income, before applying PTE or SUTE exemption schedules.
Use for the partial tax exemption schedule under s 43 (YA 2020 onwards: 75% of the first S$10,000 and 50% of the next S$190,000).
Use for the start-up tax exemption schedule under s 43 (YA 2020 onwards, first 3 YAs: 75% of the first S$100,000 and 50% of the next S$100,000), when the company meets the IRAS conditions.
Use for withholding on interest, commissions and fees in connection with a loan or indebtedness paid to a non-resident.
Use for withholding on royalties or lump sums for use of movable property paid to a non-resident.
Use for withholding on payments for use of scientific, technical, industrial or commercial knowledge or information.
Use for withholding on rent or other payments for use of movable property paid to a non-resident.
Use for withholding on technical assistance and service fees and management fees paid to a non-resident, at the prevailing corporate income tax rate.
Use for withholding on payments to a non-resident director: 22% for income due and payable from 1 January 2016 through 31 December 2022, then 24%.
Use for withholding on payments to a non-resident professional or firm.
Use for withholding on payments to a non-resident public entertainer.
Use for withholding on the sale of real property by a non-resident property trader.
Use for withholding on payments to a non-resident international market agent in the casino sector.

treatments.notes: Reported in GST F5 Box 3. Input tax attributable to exempt supplies is blocked unless the De Minimis Rule applies (IRAS: the value of exempt supplies does not exceed an average of S$40,000 a month and 5% of the total value of taxable and exempt supplies) or Regulation 33 of the GST (General) Regulations provides an exception.
